facts.fact: On 31 March 2026 Makerere University School of Public Health's METS programme signed over to the Ministry of Health 16 digital health systems it had developed, among them the UgandaEMR repositories and EMR metrics, with 725 servers and more than 4,700 computing devices.

Makerere says the systems handed over, including the electronic medical record platforms, were built over 15 years on three US Government (CDC/PEPFAR) grants totalling US$103.8 million; no domestic budget line is mentioned.

The handover of the UgandaEMR repositories and supporting infrastructure from the donor-funded Makerere METS programme to the Ministry of Health took place on 31 March 2026, the Permanent Secretary saying the country would not return to paper-heavy systems.
Makerere's METS programme reports that reporting through DHIS2 improved from 58 percent in 2020 to 98 percent in 2025; what the rate measures and its denominator are not stated.
